text:
oncall-bot: Pager duty alert: elevated error rate from CacheLynx managed cache (third-party). 5xx/429 observed in rate limiter and auth cache paths. Incident created: INC-2026-724. Root affected services: rate-limiter, token-cache, prefix-KV. First seen: 2026-08-12T03:20:10Z.

oncall-bot: Summary: CacheLynx API returning 429 and intermittent 502 on pooled connections -> causing cache miss storm, increased downstream load on primary DB and spikes in inference latency. Impact: higher tail latency and ~8% 5xx on /v1/generate for hosted customers. Paging oncall.

ravi.k: ack. I’m on it, logging in to investigate. Switched my status to "on call".

emily: seeing lots of tokencache misses in logs. Example from edge-proxy: ```
[2026-08-12T03:21:05Z] ERROR token-cache: cache call failed: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests from https://api.cachelynx.net/token-lookup
stack: CacheLookupError -> upstream 429 -> raising CacheMiss
```

cheng: similar in rate-limiter service. Redis client errors "ERR max number of connections" followed by connection resets. snippet: ```
ERR: Connection reset by peer (for host cachelynx-redis-01.cachelynx.net:6379)
WARN: fallback to local windowing - increased pass-through to backend
```

lina: Is there a provider status page? I can't find a public incident. I've opened a support ticket with CacheLynx (ticket #CL-98721) and requested priority escalation. Support replied with an automated note about "capacity pressure" in EU region.

ravi.k: Mitigations I'm putting in place now: 1) Enable local in-memory token cache fallback and extend TTL for warmed entries to reduce calls to CacheLynx; 2) Temporarily relax strict global rate limiter for known internal routes (canaries + internal health checks) to avoid cascading failures; 3) Throttle non-critical background jobs that hit cache tier. Doing step 1 now (deploying feature flag).

emily: Ravi - please add a short circuit for token lookup that returns cached deny (fail closed?) No — we should fail open for auth lookups to avoid user lockouts. Devex preference: fail permissively for already-authenticated tokens, but log.

ravi.k: Agreed. Implementing fail-open for token verification if CacheLynx returns 429/502. Pushing small change to rate-limiter cluster:```bash
./deploy canary --service rate-limiter --image redwood/rate-limiter:2026-08-12-canary-redisfall
```

pagerduty-bot: Note: alert routed to SRE oncall (ravi.k) and notified on rotation. If incident is not acknowledged in 5m escalate to ops-lead.

support-eng: I've pulled the provider logs and see connection spikes from our IP block. We should consider connection pool backoff and reducing parallelism to CacheLynx from each worker to avoid exacerbating limits. Suggest changing pool size from 50 -> 10 and enabling jittered backoff.

cheng: Rolling rate-limiter pool change to 10, will watch. Also adding small jittered exponential backoff for cache calls. Config snippet: ```json
{"cache_pool_size":10, "backoff": {"base_ms":100, "max_ms":2000, "jitter": true}}
```

emily: Customer impact note for status page draft: "We are actively mitigating an external managed cache provider issue causing increased error rates and latency for token validation and rate-limited endpoints. Some customers may see transient 5xx or increased response times. We do not believe customer data has been affected." Please keep concise.

ops-lead: Good. Add an explicit percent: initially we measured ~8% 5xx on public API, peak 12% in EU region. Include that in incident banner. Also mark Dedicated customers with private deployments as unaffected unless they depend on CacheLynx.

ravi.k: Update: local cache fallback deployed to 25% of traffic (canary). Early telemetry shows reduction in external calls to CacheLynx by ~60% for token lookups on canary shard. Rolling to 100% over 10 minutes if stable.

oncall-bot: Action checklist added to incident: triage, mitigate, contact provider, customer comms, postmortem. Assigned: ravi.k (lead), cheng (rate-limiter), emily (customer comms), lina (provider contact).

lina: CacheLynx engineer responded — they confirm "API rate limiting due to control-plane autoscaling lag in EU cluster". ETA unknown. They've applied a temporary config to throttle internal tasks and asked customers to reduce connection counts and retry rates.

support-eng: We should also rotate to our fallback provider for critical paths if possible. We have a read-only token mirror in AWS ElastiCache for some customers; triggering fallback now for auth reads. Switching traffic for 10% of requests to ElastiCache mirror as experiment.

cheng: Mirror routing started. Observability: request success for mirrored traffic ~99.8% while cachelynx traffic still ~88%. This confirms provider degradation.

emily: Draft public status update (short): "We are experiencing elevated HTTP 5xx and throttling errors due to a third-party managed cache provider (CacheLynx) affecting token validation and rate-limited endpoints. Our engineers have deployed workarounds to reduce dependence on the provider and routed some traffic to a fallback cache. We continue to monitor and coordinate with the provider." Can someone sign-off?

ops-lead: sign-off. Post to status.redwood.ai/incidents and include customer impact numbers and affected regions.

ravi.k: Update 03:40Z: Full rollout of local fallback and pool backoff completed. External calls to CacheLynx down ~85% globally. Error rate on /v1/generate down to 1.2% from 8%. Continuing to monitor.

lina: CacheLynx reports they applied a capacity fix in EU at 03:45Z and are seeing improvement. They will keep monitoring for 2 hours.

emily: Customer-facing Slack draft for affected customers: "We're aware of intermittent failures and elevated latency affecting token validation for requests routed through a third-party cache provider. We've deployed a fallback and expect reduced errors; we're working with the vendor for full remediation. No action required on your side."

ravi.k: Preparing post-incident actions: 1) Add automated pool-size throttling when upstream returns 429 to avoid thundering herd; 2) Expand fallback mirror coverage to more regions; 3) Add provider-specific health checks to routes to detect early signs; 4) Engage vendor SLA review.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-724 updated: severity reduced to SEV-2 at 03:48Z (mitigations effective). If regression, re-open to SEV-1.

ops-lead: Great work. We'll do a 30-minute sync after stabilization for a quick RCA and then schedule a formal postmortem. Please capture metrics (pre/post) and exact config changes.

ravi.k: Logging final notes here before handoff to next oncall (cheng): mitigation stable, monitoring window set for 2h, vendor engagement ongoing. Handoff at 04:15Z.

cheng: ack. I'll take the next watch and own the RCA doc. Thanks all.

oncall-bot: Incident closed for paging at 04:20:05Z — monitoring only. Remember to attach runbook steps in INC ticket and add timeline to postmortem.
